title: Unsolved to Culture
description: Compare unresolved texts, partial decipherments and archival recoveries, then explore public puzzle culture.

stops.label: Hall XII: Unsolved Ciphers
stops.note: Compare open cryptanalytic questions, unknown writing systems and unresolved interpretation; they are different kinds of uncertainty.

stops.label: Kryptos
stops.note: K1–K3 were publicly solved; K4 plaintext was found in archival papers in 2025, distinct from a public cryptanalytic solution.

stops.label: Voynich Manuscript
stops.note: A centuries-old unresolved script where language and cipher hypotheses still compete.

stops.label: Zodiac Z-13/Z-32
stops.note: Z408 and Z340 are solved; the short Z13 and Z32 fragments lack generally accepted solutions.

stops.label: Hall XIII: Cipher Culture
stops.note: See how unsolved and breakable ciphers migrate into fiction, games, and mass participation.

stops.label: Poe's Gold-Bug
stops.note: The canonical literary case where readers are taught to decode along with the story.

stops.label: Gravity Falls Ciphers
stops.note: A modern broadcast-era cipher ecosystem that trains audience codebreakers.

stops.label: Cicada 3301
stops.note: Internet-scale puzzle design blending cryptography, steganography, and culture.
